choices.text: It has been used up and destroyed
It has changed form - chemical energy became kinetic energy plus heat
It vanished because the work stopped

questions.feedback: That used-up answer is the one to unlearn: Energy gets used up when work is done. Reteach point: Energy is never used up: it changes form, like chemical energy becoming kinetic energy plus heat.
questions.misconception: Energy gets used up when work is done.
questions.prompt: A car runs out of petrol and stops. What has happened to its energy?

questions.feedback: Scene s1 fixes this: work = force x distance = 50 x 4 = 200 joules.
questions.prompt: Calculate the work done when a 50 N force pushes a crate 4 m.

questions.feedback: Scene s2: power = work / time = 200 / 2 = 100 watts - the same work in less time is more power.
questions.prompt: The same 200 J of work is done first in 10 s, then in 2 s. The power changes from 20 W to what?

questions.answer: 98 J - all the GPE has become KE; the total is unchanged.
questions.feedback: Scene s3: the total stays 98 J - nothing is lost; the GPE becomes KE as it falls.
questions.prompt: A 2 kg mass held 5 m up has 98 J of GPE. It falls to the ground. How much KE does it have just before landing, ignoring air resistance?
